border-b border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">How to Build a Telegram Bot Using Typescript & Node.js</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">21</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Dec 2022 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Eluda</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> Engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><h2 id="introduction"><a href="#introduction" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Introduction</h2> <p>In this tutorial, you’ll learn all the steps that go into building a dead-simple Telegram bot and hosting it on the cloud. It will greet people and apply ＦＡＮＣＹ text effects.</p> <p>You’ll be writing code using the Typescript language and running it on the Node.js server environment.</p> <p>And seeing as Telegram bots are built on an HTTP-based API, you’ll be using the <a href="https://grammy.dev/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">GrammY framework</a> for higher-level abstractions and a better programming experience.</p> <h3 id="prerequisites"><a href="#prerequisites" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Prerequisites</h3> <p>Before writing any code, make sure to have the following programs installed on your computer:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://telegram.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Telegram client.</a></li> <li><a href="https://nodejs.org/en/download/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Node.js</a> v14+, NPM v6+, and cURL.</li> <li>VS Code, or any other IDE of choice.</li> </ul> <p>You’ll be using <a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic</a> to host this project on the cloud, so make sure to take advantage of the Free Forever tier.</p> <p>And while you don’t have to be an expert in it, you should know a bit of Typescript. You’ll be using it to write all the code in this tutorial.</p> <h3 id="setup-the-project"><a href="#setup-the-project" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Setup the Project</h3> <p>Downloading the starter files Start-up this project by cloning the final version into your computer:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">git</span> clone https://github.com/eludadev/telegram-bot.git <span class="token builtin class-name">cd</span> telegram-bot </code></pre></div> <p>And make sure to roll it back to its very first stage, so you can learn how to build the rest of it in this tutorial:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">git</span> reset <span class="token parameter variable">--hard</span> 3ea99a5e111e84da4825b0732d76c386b5c8fdda </code></pre></div> <p>After that’s done, install the project’s dependencies:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">npm</span> <span class="token function">install</span> </code></pre></div> <h4 id="getting-your-telegram-bot-api-token"><a href="#getting-your-telegram-bot-api-token" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Getting your Telegram bot API token</h4> <p><img alt="" src="/content/botfather.access.gif"></p> <p>Using the Telegram client, start a conversation with the <a href="https://telegram.me/BotFather" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@BotFather</a>.</p> <p>Send it the following messages:</p> <ol> <li>/newbot</li> <li>Your bot name</li> <li>Your bot username (can’t contain spaces and must end in “bot”)</li> </ol> <p>After that, create a new file in the project’s root directory called <code>.env</code>. Paste the following line into that file, replacing <code><YOUR-API-TOKEN></code> with your bot’s API token that you just got from the last message with <a href="https://telegram.me/BotFather" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@BotFather</a>.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-text"><code>TELEGRAM_TOKEN=<YOUR-API-TOKEN> </code></pre></div> <h4 id="initializing-the-telegram-bot"><a href="#initializing-the-telegram-bot" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Initializing the Telegram bot</h4> <p>Create a new file called <code>bot.ts</code> in the <code>src/</code> directory. That’s where you’ll be writing code for the rest of this tutorial.</p> <p>You’ll be using the <a href="https://grammy.dev/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">GrammY framework</a> to build this bot; it’s much easier this way instead of interacting directly with the <a href="https://core.telegram.org/bots/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">API routes</a>.</p> <p>Head into the bot script and import the library in question:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">import</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> Bot <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token keyword">from</span> <span class="token string">"grammy"</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token comment">// Create a bot using the Telegram token</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> bot <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword">new</span> <span class="token class-name">Bot</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>process<span class="token punctuation">.</span>env<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token constant">TELEGRAM_TOKEN</span> <span class="token operator">||</span> <span class="token string">""</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>As you can see, the bot is created with the <code>TELEGRAM_TOKEN</code> variable that you just set in the <code>.env</code> file. After that, handle all message events by responding with a friendly robot introduction:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">const</span> introductionMessage <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">Hello! I'm a Telegram bot. I'm powered by Cyclic, the next-generation serverless computing platform.
<b>Commands</b> /yo - Be greeted by me /effect [text] - Show a keyboard to apply text effects to [text]</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> <span class="token function-variable function">replyWithIntro</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span>ctx<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token builtin">any</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">=></span> ctx<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">reply</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>introductionMessage<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> parse_mode<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"HTML"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">on</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"message"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> replyWithIntro<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Take note of the <code>parse_mode</code> parameter. It’s used to allow HTML tags in the message response, such as <code><b>Commands</b></code>.</p> <p>And finally, start-up the bot by running one method:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code>bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">start</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Follow that by executing the bot script:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">npm</span> run dev </code></pre></div> <p><img alt="" src="/content/botfather.newbot.png"></p> <p>And boom! You’ve got yourself a dead-simple bot running on your computer. You can test-it out by sending it a message on Telegram; you may want to follow the link previously given to you by <a href="https://telegram.me/BotFather" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@BotFather</a>.</p> <h2 id="handle-basic-commands"><a href="#handle-basic-commands" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Handle basic commands</h2> <p><img alt="" src="/content/botcommands.basic.gif"> Telegram bots can handle commands, which aren’t much different from ordinary messages. The syntax for such interactions follows the following format:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code>bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">command</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"start"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> replyWithIntro<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Test it out by sending the <code>/start</code> message to your bot. Note that your program is automatically updated once you modify the bot script.</p> <p>After that’s done, modify your bot to handle the <code>/yo</code> command. It will simply respond with the username of the sender:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token comment">// Handle the /yo command to greet the user</span> bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">command</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"yo"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span>ctx<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">=></span> ctx<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">reply</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">Yo </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>ctx<span class="token punctuation">.</span>from<span class="token operator">?.</span>username<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>And since the <code>bot.on(“message”)</code> event handler is on top, it will catch all messages and the /start and /yo commands won’t have an effect. Please make sure to always keep it at the bottom of the file:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token comment">// Keep this at the bottom of the file</span> bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">on</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"message"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> replyWithIntro<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <h2 id="build-inline-keyboards"><a href="#build-inline-keyboards" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Build Inline Keyboards</h2> <p>Telegram bots can also respond with a set of buttons underneath the message. Let’s do a simple demonstration. Change the introductory response to also contain a button that links users to the <a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic</a> website, the platform that we’ll use to deploy our bot to the cloud for free at the end of this tutorial:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">import</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> InlineKeyboard <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token keyword">from</span> <span class="token string">"grammy"</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> aboutUrlKeyboard <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword">new</span> <span class="token class-name">InlineKeyboard</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">url</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span> <span class="token string">"Host your own bot for free."</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token string">"https://cyclic.sh/"</span> <span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> <span class="token function-variable function">replyWithIntro</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span>ctx<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token builtin">any</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">=></span> ctx<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">reply</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>introductionMessage<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> reply_markup<span class="token operator">:</span> aboutUrlKeyboard<span class="token punctuation">,</span> parse_mode<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"HTML"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>After this step, you may want to re-execute the bot script after interrupting it with the <code>Ctrl+C</code> keyboard combination:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">npm</span> run dev </code></pre></div> <h4 id="a-more-advanced-example"><a href="#a-more-advanced-example" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>A more advanced example</h4> <p><img alt="" src="/content/advancedcommands.bot.gif"> Let’s now do a more advanced example. Let’s use this to allow users to apply text effects in any conversation using your bot.</p> <h4 id="enabling-inline-mode-for-your-telegram-bot"><a href="#enabling-inline-mode-for-your-telegram-bot" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Enabling inline mode for your Telegram bot</h4> <p><img alt="" src="/content/enableinlinemode.bot.gif"></p> <p>By default, this feature comes disabled. Contact <a href="https://telegram.me/BotFather" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@BotFather</a> to enable it:</p> <ol> <li>/mybots</li> <li>Select your bot from the inline keyboard</li> <li>Bot settings</li> <li>Inline mode</li> <li>Turn on</li> </ol> <p>Handling the “effect” inline query Inline queries are generally handled by matching a RegEx pattern. punctuation">(</span>queryRegEx<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">if</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token operator">!</span>fullQueryMatch<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">return</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> effectLabel <span class="token operator">=</span> fullQueryMatch<span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token number">1</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> originalText <span class="token operator">=</span> fullQueryMatch<span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token number">2</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> effectCode <span class="token operator">=</span> allEffects<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">find</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span>effect<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">=></span> effect<span class="token punctuation">.</span>label<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">toLowerCase</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">===</span> effectLabel<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">toLowerCase</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token operator">?.</span>code<span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> modifiedText <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">applyTextEffect</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>originalText<span class="token punctuation">,</span> effectCode <span class="token keyword">as</span> Variant<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">await</span> ctx<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">answerInlineQuery</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span> <span class="token punctuation">[</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> type<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"article"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> id<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"text-effect"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> title<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"Text Effects"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> input_message_content<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> message_text<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">Original: </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>originalText<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string"> Modified: </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>modifiedText<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> parse_mode<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"HTML"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> reply_markup<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token keyword">new</span> <span class="token class-name">InlineKeyboard</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">switchInline</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"Share"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> fullQuery<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> url<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"http://t.me/EludaDevSmarterBot"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> description<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"Create stylish Unicode text, all within Telegram."</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> cache_time<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token number">30</span> <span class="token operator">*</span> <span class="token number">24</span> <span class="token operator">*</span> <span class="token number">3600</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token comment">// one month in seconds</span> <span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <h2 id="polish-the-telegram-bot"><a href="#polish-the-telegram-bot" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Polish the Telegram Bot</h2> <p><img alt="" src="/content/polishthebot.png"></p> <p>It’s often useful for Telegram bots to display a list of supported commands, and while we’re already doing that in the introductory message, there’s a more formal way of doing so, and it’s as simple as one command:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token comment">// Suggest commands in the menu</span> bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span>api<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">setMyCommands</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">[</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> command<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"yo"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> description<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"Be greeted by the bot"</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> command<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"effect"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> description<span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"Apply text effects on the text. (usage: /effect [text])"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Note that to see the new menu, you must restart your Telegram client.</p> <p>Furthermore, professional bots come with a profile picture and a well-formed description. You can do all of that by contacting <a href="https://telegram.me/BotFather" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@BotFather</a>:</p> <ol> <li>Edit bot</li> <li>Edit about / Edit description / Edit botpic</li> </ol> <h2 id="deploy-the-telegram-bot-to-the-cloud"><a href="#deploy-the-telegram-bot-to-the-cloud" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Deploy the Telegram Bot to the Cloud</h2> <h4 id="long-polling-vs-webhooks"><a href="#long-polling-vs-webhooks" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Long Polling vs Webhooks</h4> <p>There are two fundamentally different ways of deploying your Telegram bot to the web.</p> <p>The first one is <a href="https://grammy.dev/guide/deployment-types.html#how-does-long-polling-work" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Long Polling</a>, and we’ve already been using it in this tutorial by running <code>bot.start()</code>. With it, bots constantly send requests to the Telegram servers checking for new messages, and responding to them accordingly.</p> <p>This approach is not compatible with the serverless architecture, as the latter expects applications to only run once, and only on-demand.</p> <p>“Serverless means applications are only on for the time it takes to process individual requests. They are suspended immediately after each response is sent.” — <a href="https://docs.cyclic.sh/serverless/on-demand" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic docs</a>.</p> <p>The solution to this problem is deployment by <a href="https://grammy.dev/guide/deployment-types.html#how-do-webhooks-work" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Webhooks</a>, an alternative strategy that makes the Telegram client itself contact your bot when there’s a new message. And while this comes with <a href="https://grammy.dev/guide/deployment-types.html#webhook-reply" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">its own drawbacks</a>, it’s fully compatible with serverless architecture.</p> <h4 id="using-webhooks-for-deployment"><a href="#using-webhooks-for-deployment" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Using Webhooks for deployment</h4> <p>By following the <code>NODE_ENV</code> environment variable, we can tell whether the bot instance is running in a development or a production stage. Replace the <code>bot.start()</code> command with the following:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">import</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> webhookCallback <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token keyword">from</span> <span class="token string">"grammy"</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">import</span> express <span class="token keyword">from</span> <span class="token string">"express"</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token comment">// Start the server</span> <span class="token keyword">if</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span>process<span class="token punctuation">.</span>env<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token constant">NODE_ENV</span> <span class="token operator">===</span> <span class="token string">"production"</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// Use Webhooks for the production server</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> app <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">express</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">use</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>express<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">json</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">use</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token function">webhookCallback</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>bot<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token string">"express"</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> <span class="token constant">PORT</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> process<span class="token punctuation">.</span>env<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token constant">PORT</span> <span class="token operator">||</span> <span class="token number">3000</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">listen</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token constant">PORT</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token builtin">console</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">log</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">Bot listening on port </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span><span class="token constant">PORT</span><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token keyword">else</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// Use Long Polling for development</span> bot<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token function">start</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <h4 id="pushing-all-files-to-a-github-repository"><a href="#pushing-all-files-to-a-github-repository" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Pushing all files to a Github Repository</h4> <p>It’s imperative that we use a Github repository to store our bot files so we can deploy it to the cloud. After <a href="https://github.com/new" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">creating a new repository</a> (either public or private), run the following commands to link it with your local Git instance, replacing <code><YOUR-GH-REPO-LINK></code> with your repo’s URL:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token builtin class-name">export</span> <span class="token assign-left variable">GH_REPO</span><span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">"<YOUR-GH-REPO-LINK>"</span> <span class="token function">git</span> remote remove origin <span class="token function">git</span> remote <span class="token function">add</span> origin <span class="token string">"<span class="token variable">$GH_REPO</span>.git"</span> </code></pre></div> <p>After that, stage, commit, and push your files to the new remote origin:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">git</span> <span class="token function">add</span> <span class="token builtin class-name">.</span> <span class="token function">git</span> commit <span class="token parameter variable">-m</span> <span class="token string">"Build the Telegram bot."</span> <span class="token function">git</span> branch <span class="token parameter variable">-M</span> main <span class="token function">git</span> push origin main </code></pre></div> <h4 id="deploying-for-free-using-cyclic"><a href="#deploying-for-free-using-cyclic" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Deploying for free using Cyclic</h4> <p>After creating your Cyclic account, use it to deploy your new Telegram bot. It’s free forever, and no credit card is required.</p> <p>Note that you must sign up using the same Github account that you used to create your bot’s repository.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/deploywithcyclic.bot.gif"></p> <p>Open your <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/#/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic dashboard</a>, click on the Deploy button and switch to the “Link your own” tab. Search for your bot’s repo and click on the “Connect” button. Then sit back and watch it do all the work for you!</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/editvariables.bot.gif"></p> <p>The final step is setting the same environment variables as you did in the <code>.env</code> file. Open your Cyclic deployment’s dashboard page, switch to the Variables page and set the appropriate values for the environment variables:</p> <ul> <li>NODE_ENV: production</li> <li>TELEGRAM_TOKEN: your bot’s API token (same as <code>.env</code> file)</li> </ul> <h4 id="connecting-your-telegram-bot-to-your-cyclic-server"><a href="#connecting-your-telegram-bot-to-your-cyclic-server" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Connecting your Telegram bot to your Cyclic server</h4> <p><img alt="" src="/content/connecttelegram.png"></p> <p>You want to tell Telegram to send the Webhook requests to your Cyclic server. So conclude this project by copying your Cyclic deployment’s URL and running these commands:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token builtin class-name">export</span> <span class="token assign-left variable">TELEGRAM_API_TOKEN</span><span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token punctuation">..</span>. <span class="token comment"># YOUR TELEGRAM API TOKEN</span> <span class="token builtin class-name">export</span> <span class="token assign-left variable">TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL</span><span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token punctuation">..</span>. <span class="token comment"># YOUR CYCLIC DEPLOYMENT URL</span>
<span class="token function">curl</span> <span class="token string">"https://api.telegram.org/bot<span class="token variable">$TELEGRAM_API_TOKEN</span>/setWebhook?url=<span class="token variable">$TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL</span>"</span> </code></pre></div> <p>And boom! Your bot’s now actively running on the cloud! You may stop your local development instance by pressing <code>Ctrl+C</code> and notice how your bot is still working.</p> <h2 id="conclusion"><a href="#conclusion" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Conclusion</h2> <p>You’ve successfully reached the end of this tutorial! There are many more things you could add to this bot, including but not limited to games, error handling and internationalization.</p> <p>You may also want to learn more about Telegram bots:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://grammy.dev/guide/inline-queries.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://grammy.dev/guide/inline-queries.html</a></li> <li><a href="https://grammy.dev/plugins/keyboard.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://grammy.dev/plugins/keyboard.html</a></li> <li><a href="https://grammy.dev/guide/deployment-types.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://grammy.dev/guide/deployment-types.html</a></li> </ul> <p>And here are some resources to advance your knowledge about serverless computing:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/vs-heroku" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic vs Heroku</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/considerations-for-serverless-active-active-routing/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Considerations for Serverless Active-Active: Routing</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/how-to-fail-at-serverless-serverless-is-stateless/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How to Fail at Serverless: Serverless is Stateless</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.cyclic.sh/tutorials/rest-api-and-dynamodb/part-1" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Creating and Deploying a RESTful API on Serverless Infrastructure</a></li> </ul></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%] px-7 py-10 bg-neutral-800/20"><div class="flex flex-col items-center text-center"><h2 class="font-bold text-4xl mb-4">Subscribe to posts</h2> <p>Enter your email If you would like to get an email the next time we post.<br>We post about ~1-2x per month, and up to once a month about company news.<br></p></div> <div class="mt-4"><div id="embedded-form"></div></div></section> <div class="relative w-full bg-neutral-800/20 border !border-neutral-700 rounded-xl flex flex-col items-center gap-5 text-center p-8"><h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Launch a hello world</h2> <p class="w-full md:w-[50%] text-neutral-300"> Fork and deploy a hello world project onto Cyclic faster than it has taken to read this page. Experience the power. </p> <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/api/login" target="_blank" class="bg-primary text-white capitalize flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl px-4 py-3 gap-2 hover:no-underline hover:scale-105 transition w-full md:w-max"> Deploy on Cyclic 🚀 </a></div></section> <footer class="border-t border-white/20 py-16 px-6 sm:px-0 bg-black/20 backdrop-blur"><div border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">The Modern Refresher to React Development in 2022</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">24</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Aug 2022 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Eluda</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> Engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><h1 id="the-modern-refresher-to-react-development-in-2022"><a href="#the-modern-refresher-to-react-development-in-2022" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>The Modern Refresher to React Development in 2022</h1> <p>There's no denying that React is the most popular web framework out there. This fact is even proven by StackOverFlow's recent survey polling hundreds of thousands of developers.</p> <p><img alt="top-wanted-frameworks.png" src="/content/react-dev-2022/top-wanted-frameworks.png"></p> <p>Having already covered <a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/i-made-the-same-app-3-times-in-3-different-frameworks-heres-what-i-learned" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Vue development in our prior article in this series</a> comparing web frameworks, it's only fair to give React an equal chance of showing-off its features and community-made treasures.</p> <p>And while React is backed by multi-trillion dollar company, Meta (or Facebook), it's <a href="https://github.com/facebook/react" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">open-source community</a> is still one of the key factors of its large success. In this article, we'll go through the React development process for beginners and developers who just need a quick refresher.</p> <p>We'll build a <a href="https://ithink-react.cyclic.app/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">website for publicly sharing short-messages, called</a> <strong><a href="https://ithink.cyclic.app/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">"ithink"</a></strong>. It's like Twitter, but with no accounts and you can't delete what you post.</p> <p><a href="https://github.com/ithink-corp/react" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://github.com/ithink-corp/react</a></p> <h2 id="first-we-need-an-api"><a href="#first-we-need-an-api" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>First, we need an API</h2> <p>If you play around with the CodePen above, you'll quickly realize that the database is not fake.</p> <p>We actually have a <a href="https://github.com/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">back-end side of our application</a>: it handles the storing and retrieving of simple text data. It's also built on <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/s3/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon's S3</a> object storage service.</p> <p><a href="https://github.com/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://github.com/ithink-corp/api</a></p> <p>A developer would normally spend hours and hours setting-up a database like this, and it's not free either. Luckily for us, we get a free instance of the AWS S3 Storage when we <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/#/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">use Cyclic</a>. No credit card is required.</p> <p><a href="https://deploy.cyclic.app/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><img alt="Deploy to Cyclic Button" src="https://deploy.cyclic.app/button.svg"></a></p> <h2 id="how-do-we-create-a-new-react-project"><a href="#how-do-we-create-a-new-react-project" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>How do we create a new React project?</h2> <p>A beginner shouldn't have to create <em>anything</em> from scratch.</p> <p>That's a fact, and the React community recognizes it so much that they built a completely interactive program that helps newcomers setup their projects without much hassle.</p> <p><img alt="create-react-app.svg" src="/content/react-dev-2022/create-react-app.svg"></p> <p>It's called <code>create-react-app</code>, and it uses <a href="https://babeljs.io/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Babel</a> and <a href="https://webpack.js.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">webpack</a> under the hood, but you don't need to know anything about them. But I'd be irresponsible if I told you that you'll never encounter these two programs, so I recommend saving these articles <a href="https://dev.to/anitaparmar26/webpack-5-guide-for-beginners-314c" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">about webpack</a> and <a href="https://www.sitepoint.com/babel-beginners-guide/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Babel</a>. Read them when you're ready.</p> <p>It's finally time to use this magical software. Make sure that you <a href="https://nodejs.org/en/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">have NodeJS and NPM installed on your machine</a>, then launch your terminal and run the following command in your preferred directory:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code>npx create-react-app my-app <span class="token builtin class-name">cd</span> my-app <span class="token function">npm</span> start </code></pre></div> <p>If you're not using Linux or MacOS for programming, check out this <a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/linux-vs-windows-commands/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">cheat-sheet covering our commands' counter-parts in Windows</a>.</p> <p>Don't worry if it takes unusually long for these commands to execute. They may take longer to run if you have a slower internet connection. Please give it some time, as you only need to run it once per project.</p> <p><br><br> <video src="/content/react-dev-2022/Scroll_Capture_2022-08-10_at_8.34.52_PM.webm" playsinline="true" autoplay muted loop style="max-width:730px"></video> <br><br></p> <p>When these commands finally cease to run, a new tab will automatically open in your current web browser. While not much, the source-code behind it is critical to the development that we're gonna do in this article.</p> <p>Regardless of what starter is given to us when we run <code>create-react-app</code>, the first step is to actually erase all of it. Yes, you heard me correctly; we're gonna erase <em>almost</em> all of what this magical program does.</p> <p>But don't fret, the part that we're gonna delete is not the useful part of the React template, so go ahead and run this command:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">rm</span> src/* <span class="token parameter variable">-r</span> <span class="token comment"># erase all files in the src/ folder</span> <span class="token function">touch</span> src/index.js <span class="token comment"># create a new file called "index.js" in the src/ folder</span> </code></pre></div> <p>We already did too much change, but we can go a step further and craft our own folders. A good folder structure is key to a well-organized and future-proof project. There are many <a href="https://reactjs.org/docs/faq-structure.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">not-so-well-agreed-on candidates</a> out there, but we're gonna go simple and create only two new directories:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">mkdir</span> src/components src/utils <span class="token comment"># create two directories in the src/ folder</span> </code></pre></div> <p>As their name suggests, <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model%E2%80%93view%E2%80%93controller" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">components</a> (like the pop-up modal) will go into the <code>components/</code> folder, and useful functions (like a function to post data to the server) will go into the <code>utils/</code> sibling.</p> <p>Another step that we would do in this stage is to set-up <a href="https://tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/create-react-app" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">TailwindCSS</a> and <a href="https://fontawesome.com/docs/web/use-with/react/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">FontAwesome</a> as they're used in this project. These packages both contain <em>detailed</em> guides that will help you set them up for yourself. This is just another consequence of the wide popularity of React.</p> <p>No beginner tutorial covers this, but there's a little secret in programming that you should start practicing as soon as possible. It's the use of <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lint_(software)" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">linters</a>, programs that enforce <a href="https://airbnb.io/javascript/react/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">style-guides in your code</a> and catch bugs before they happen. I recommend using <a href="https://eslint.org/docs/latest/user-guide/getting-started" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><code>eslint</code></a>, the most popular linter in the JavaScript world. Setting-it up is easy, as covering in the linked guide.</p> <h2 id="how-do-we-create-a-component-in-react"><a href="#how-do-we-create-a-component-in-react" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>How do we create a component in React?</h2> <p data-height="300" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="zYWJENQ" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:300px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/zYWJENQ"> React ithink 1</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span> </p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <p>As it currently stands, our app is not functional. This stems from the fact that the <code>index.js</code> script is still empty, and that's because we just created it.</p> <p>Let's learn a new fact about React: each application must have <em>one</em> <strong>main component</strong>. It's like the <code><body></code> element, where all the content is held. React places the insides of the main component inside a top-level <code>#root</code> element, as you can see in the following image:</p> <p><img alt="Screenshot from 2022-08-10 22-42-22.png" src="/content/react-dev-2022/Screenshot_from_2022-08-10_22-42-22.png"></p> <p>As you might have guessed, we create this main component inside the <code>index.js</code> file. Those are a lot of new things that you may have never seen before. First of all, there's the presence of <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">imports</a> and <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">classes</a>. Please make sure that your understanding of these two concepts is rock-solid before continuing with this article.</p> <p>But there's one other thing that still stands out, and it's surely new to all beginner React developers. It's the "weird" mix of JavaScript code and HTML markup. This odd format is called <a href="https://reactjs.org/docs/introducing-jsx.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">JSX</a>, the <strong>J</strong>ava<strong>S</strong>cript E<strong>x</strong>tension. All you need to know about it for now is that it makes the inclusion of HTML markup inside JavaScript code okay.</p> <ul> <li> <p><strong>It doesn't always work!</strong></p> <p>With JSX, this is It's recommended to define component methods in the following manner:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token comment">// Bad! :(</span> <span class="token function">toggleModal</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// do stuff...</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span>
<span class="token comment">// Okay :)</span> <span class="token function-variable function">toggleModal</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// do stuff...</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Long story short, the first style would prohibit your method from accessing the <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/this" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><code>this</code> keyword</a>, which you would need to alter other parts of the component. On the other hand, the second method is fine and you should make it a habit to define class methods in that style.</p> <h2 id="how-do-we-create-a-toggle-in-react"><a href="#how-do-we-create-a-toggle-in-react" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>How do we create a toggle in React?</h2> <p>Almost every user-interface component has one or more toggles in it, and our pop-up modal is no different. With a Boolean toggle, we can dictate if the modal is either open or closed. Thankfully, creating toggles is no hassle at all.</p> <p>Variables that control the UI are all collectively called the <strong>state</strong>, and our modal toggle is clearly one of them. The state is anything from data displayed in the application to user input to toggles that can do pretty much everything. When a state variable changes, the component is quickly and efficiently refreshed. Creating stateful variables is also the easiest thing in the world:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token function">constructor</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">props</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">super</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>props<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">this</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">state</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">isModalOpen</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Toggles wouldn't be very interesting if we couldn't actually <em>toggle</em> them. This logic falls into the component method that we created earlier. Unfortunately, mutating stateful variables is quite counter-intuitive:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token function-variable function">toggleModal</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// Wrong! :(</span> <span class="token keyword">this</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">state</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">isModalOpen</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">true</span>

<span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token method function property-access">render</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">return</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>div</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token plain-text"> ... </span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span><span class="token class-name">Modal</span></span> <span class="token punctuation">/></span></span><span class="token plain-text"> </span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>div</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>We also can't forget about the toggle logic that we just implemented in the last section of this article, so we must put it to use. It's easy to tell React to <em>conditionally</em> show an element based on a Boolean <strong>state variable</strong>. The syntax that I'm about to introduce is quite new, and it's special to <strong>JSX</strong>:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">this</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">state</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">isModalOpen</span> <span class="token operator">&&</span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span><span class="token class-name">Modal</span></span><span class="token punctuation">/></span></span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>The double brackets are key to combining JavaScript logic with HTML markup. They can contain <em>almost</em> anything from calculations to String manipulations and even lists of HTML elements as we'll soon see in this guide:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token string">'Hello'</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token number">5</span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token number">5</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token string">'Hello'</span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token string">' World'</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>This neat feature of JSX is called <strong><a href="https://egghead.io/lessons/react-understand-and-use-interpolation-in-jsx" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" Thankfully, this is not very different from former server function that we just implemented.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token function">constructor</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">props</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">super</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>props<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">this</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">state</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">messages</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token keyword null nil">null</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>As soon as the main component is created, we wish to load data from the server. There's no immediately obvious way of implementing this logic, because you still don't know about <strong><a href="https://reactjs.org/docs/state-and-lifecycle.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">lifecycle hooks</a></strong>. With these magical devices, we're able to run whatever logic we want at important times in a component's "lifecycle".</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token method function property-access">componentDidMount</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// load items</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>With the <code>compnentDidMount</code> lifecycle hook, we're able to run whatever we want when the component is finally rendered, which is exactly what we were looking for. With that done, we're left with the task of filling the <code>messages</code> <strong>stateful variable</strong> with data from the server.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> getMessages <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'./utils/server'</span>
<span class="token keyword">class</span> <span class="token class-name">App</span> <span class="token keyword">extends</span> <span class="token class-name">React<span class="token punctuation">.</span>Component</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token spread operator">...</span> <span class="token method function property-access">componentDidMount</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> messages <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">await</span> <span class="token function">getMessages</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">this</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">setState</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">messages</span><span class="token operator">:</span> messages<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Of course, we cannot dismiss the logic that actually retrieves data from the server.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token comment">// utils/server.js</span>
<span class="token keyword module">export</span> <span class="token keyword">async</span> <span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">getMessages</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> res <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">await</span> <span class="token function">fetch</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'https://ithink-api.cyclic.app/'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">headers</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token string-property property">'Content-Type'</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">'application/json'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> items <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">await</span> res<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">json</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">return</span> items<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">map</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">item</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">message</span><span class="token operator">:</span> item<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <h2 id="how-do-we-deploy-a-react-project-to-the-internet"><a href="#how-do-we-deploy-a-react-project-to-the-internet" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>How do we deploy a React project to the Internet?</h2> <p>It's hard-enough to create an entire application in one's local computer, it's its own industry with the name: "<strong>Frontend Development</strong>". A frontend developer should not have to worry about the intricacies behind servers and deployment.</p> <p>Lucky for us, Cyclic gives us the ability to deploy React applications to the cloud for free, by just clicking one button and adding one script to our application. With <a href="https://github.com/cyclic-software/starter-react-app" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cyclic's React starter</a>, we know to add the following script to the root of our project:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-jsx"><code><span class="token comment">// /server.js</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> express <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">require</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'express'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> path <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">require</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"path"</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> app <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">express</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token comment">// This configures static hosting for files in /public that have the extensions</span> <span class="token comment">// listed in the array.</span> <span class="token keyword">var</span> options <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">dotfiles</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">'ignore'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">etag</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">extensions</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token string">'htm'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token string">'html'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'css'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'js'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'ico'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'jpg'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'jpeg'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'png'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'svg'</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">index</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token string">'index.html'</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">maxAge</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">'1m'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">redirect</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">use</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>express<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">static</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'build'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> options<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> port <span class="token operator">=</span> process<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">env</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token constant">PORT</span> <span class="token operator">||</span> <span class="token number">3000</span>
app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">listen</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>port<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token console class-name">console</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">log</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">React app listening at http://localhost:</span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>port<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> </code></pre></div> <p>It's also important to add the following changes to the <code>package.json</code> file:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-json"><code><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token property">"scripts"</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> - <span class="token property">"start"</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"react-scripts start"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> + <span class="token property">"start"</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"node server.js"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> + <span class="token property">"dev"</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">"react-scripts start"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p><br><br> <video src="/content/react-dev-2022/output.mp4" controls style="max-width:730px"></video> <br><br></p> <p>With that done, all it takes to launch our app to the world-wide-web is creating a Cyclic account and clicking the <strong>DEPLOY</strong> button. Trust me, it's so satisfying seeing it do all the work <em>for you!</em> And you can even choose your own free subdomain afterwards! 😃</p> <p><a href="https://deploy.cyclic.app/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><img alt="Deploy to Cyclic Button" src="https://deploy.cyclic.app/button.svg"></a></p> <h2 id="conclusion"><a href="#conclusion" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Conclusion</h2> <p>And voila, our application is done, just like that! The React development process is definitely a unique one, and you can immediately tell many differences from the <a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/i-made-the-same-app-3-times-in-3-different-frameworks-heres-what-i-learned" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">VueJS process that we covered in our last article</a>.</p> <p>We covered many features of React:</p> <ul> <li>Creating new projects with <code>create-react-app</code>,</li> <li>listening to and handling events,</li> <li>hooks and the react-use library,</li> <li>custom components,</li> <li>JSX interpolation,</li> <li>stateful variables,</li> <li>dynamic lists.</li> <li>DOM refs.</li> </ul> <p>And while we just scraped the surface of what React is capable of, we still got a good idea of what the React development process is like and that's enough to help us choose the best framework for our purposes.</p></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%] px-7 py-10 bg-neutral-800/20"><div class="flex flex-col items-center text-center"><h2 class="font-bold text-4xl mb-4">Subscribe to posts</h2> <p>Enter your email If you would like to get an email the next time we post.<br>We post about ~1-2x per month, and up to once a month about company news.<br></p></div> <div class="mt-4"><div id="embedded-form"></div></div></section> <div class="relative w-full bg-neutral-800/20 border !border-neutral-700 rounded-xl flex flex-col items-center gap-5 text-center p-8"><h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Launch a hello world</h2> <p class="w-full md:w-[50%] text-neutral-300"> Fork and deploy a hello world project onto Cyclic faster than it has taken to read this page. Experience the power. </p> <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/api/login" target="_blank" class="bg-primary text-white capitalize flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl px-4 py-3 gap-2 hover:no-underline hover:scale-105 transition w-full md:w-max"> Deploy on Cyclic 🚀 </a></div></section> <footer class="border-t border-white/20 py-16 px-6 sm:px-0 bg-black/20 backdrop-blur"><div
