border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">27</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Sep 2022 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Kam Lasater</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> Engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><p>When I was a younger I went on several rock climbing and mountaineering expeditions. I was exposed to some instructors and practitioners that took staying safe in the mountains very seriously. One of them carried a book from The American Alpine Club on climbing accidents. The accidents were never the cause of a single bad choice. They were caused by a series of decisions, taken over time, that combined to create the conditions for the accident.</p> <p>What stuck in my memory, sitting beside rock faces that could very well be the scene for one of the stories, was that in certain cases we might make one of the same choices. That given a different time of day, or different weather, or different climbing partners, the same choice could have different levels of risk. Reading and discussing those stories made me a more aware adventurer and a safer climber.</p> <p>The public analysis and discussion of the chain of decisions and events that led to accidents helps beginners build experience, experts grow wisdom and fosters a culture of safety. Other industries and sub-cultures, to a have their own ways to learn from accidents. For example: the US military has after action reviews, medicine has accident review boards and aviation has NTSB accident reviews.</p> <p>I have read root cause analysis reports from outages at hyper scalar cloud hosting providers. Often they read like the plaster foot prints of a long dead animal, the legal and marketing departments sanitizing and scrubing any element of life or learning from them. They are the cargo culting of accident investigation and reporting. All of the motions and affectation with none of the substance.</p> <p>The prevailing culture in software to errors seems to be "if you just". Where errors are blamed on lack of knowledge. If the operator had "just" known the impact of config change, if the developer had "just" understood the interaction of their code change. It is a culture of expert knowledge. It is based on the unexamined belief that bugs only exist from lack of knowledge or lack of care. Or taken to their offensive extremes: stupidity and laziness.</p> <p>In the software industry bugs or outages most often do not result in injury or death. However, as society becomes more dependent on the software systems we are building the severity and impact of problems only grows. As our software systems continue to grow in complexity and the reach of problems we write software to solve, we as a society must grapple with changing this culture.</p> <p>As a step on this path of changing this culture I am talking about failures I have seen or participated in. My goal is to make it easier for others to share where they have failed. This will create a feedback loop that will let us learn faster.</p> <p>Join me in sharing stories of failure. Here are some talks and posts about failure from myself and Cyclic:</p> <ol> <li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kRVUEYPua4A&t=7870s" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How to fail at Serverless (DevOpsDays Boston 2022 Conference video</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/how-to-fail-at-serverless-serverless-is-stateless/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">How to Fail at Serverless: Serverless is Stateless (blog post)</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/its-always-sunny-in-us-east-1/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Its Always Sunny in us-east-1: The gang does business continuity (blog post)</a></li> <li><a href="https://www.cyclic.sh/posts/aws-s3-why-sometimes-you-should-press-the-100k-dollar-button/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">AWS S3: Why sometimes you should press the $100k button (blog post)</a></li> </ol> <p>We would love to hear your stories.</p> <p>Write something up.</p> <p>Post it publicly.</p> <p>Let us know.</p> <p>We got your back :)</p></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%] px-7 py-10 bg-neutral-800/20"><div class="flex flex-col items-center text-center"><h2 class="font-bold text-4xl mb-4">Subscribe to posts</h2> <p>Enter your email If you would like to get an email the next time we post.<br>We post about ~1-2x per month, and up to once a month about company news.<br></p></div> <div class="mt-4"><div id="embedded-form"></div></div></section> <div class="relative w-full bg-neutral-800/20 border !border-neutral-700 rounded-xl flex flex-col items-center gap-5 text-center p-8"><h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Launch a hello world</h2> <p class="w-full md:w-[50%] text-neutral-300"> Fork and deploy a hello world project onto Cyclic faster than it has taken to read this page. Experience the power. </p> <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/api/login" target="_blank" class="bg-primary text-white capitalize flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl px-4 py-3 gap-2 hover:no-underline hover:scale-105 transition w-full md:w-max"> Deploy on Cyclic 🚀 </a></div></section> <footer class="border-t border-white/20 py-16 px-6 sm:px-0 bg-black/20 backdrop-blur"><div Here's What I Learned." sizes="(max-width: 640px) 340px, (max-width: 768px) 400px, (max-width: 1024px) 600px, 1200px" srcset="/_nuxt/image/20c713.webp 340w, /_nuxt/image/9cddfc.webp 400w, /_nuxt/image/dfb3ef.webp 600w, /_nuxt/image/1fd166.webp 1200w" class="w-full rounded-2xl"> <div class="space-y-8 border-b border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">I Made The Same App 3 Times in 3 Different Frameworks... Here's What I Learned.</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">26</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Jul 2022 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Eluda</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> Engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><p>Angular, Svelte, Solid, React, Vue — there are so many frameworks out there. And you probably dealt with <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/webdev/comments/ux2ov8/how_do_you_guys_determine_which_frameworks_to_use/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">the "framework dilemma"</a> at some point in your career.</p> <p>Some of us pursue React, the <a href="https://insights.stackoverflow.com/survey/2021#most-loved-dreaded-and-wanted-webframe-want" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">most popular framework</a>. And that's completely understandable, because it being famous also implies that it's the most demanded skill in the job market.</p> <p>Next up is Vue, and its second position in the popularity spectrum. Some people prefer Vue for the fact that it's so lightweight and yet so scalable, and others love its simplicity and similarity to other frameworks.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/62d6d1173d02703377a9cef3_top-liked-frameworks.png"></p> <p>Let's take a leap of faith and change our selection criteria from popularity to likability.</p> <p>Svelte is the most loved framework, and for good reason. Svelte places strong emphasis on developer happiness because it's so easy to pick up and has a compiler that is more efficient than its peers.</p> <p>I always wondered how different it would be to build the <strong>same app</strong> with the same features, but in <strong>3 different frameworks</strong>. For each one, I want to answer the following questions:</p> <ul> <li>How many errors will I encounter?</li> <li>How much code is there to write?</li> <li>How long does it take to build?</li> </ul> <p>We'll be exploring each of the aforementioned frameworks in its own piece, as part of a four-article series.</p> <p>We'll build a <a href="https://ithink.cyclic.app/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">website for publicly sharing short-messages, called <strong>"ithink"</strong></a>. It's like Twitter, but with no accounts and you can't delete what you post.</p> <p>‍</p><p data-height="600" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="gOerqjg" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:600px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/gOerqjg"> It's Twitter, but you can't delete.</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span></p> <p></p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <h2 id="but-first-we-need-an-api"><a href="#but-first-we-need-an-api" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>But first, we need an API</h2> <p>If you play around with the CodePen above, you'll quickly realize that the database is not fake.</p> <p>We actually have a <a href="https://github.com/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">back-end side of our application</a>: it handles the storing and retrieving of simple text data. It's also built on <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/s3/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Amazon's S3</a> object storage service.</p> <p>A developer would normally spend hours and hours setting-up a database like this, and it's not free either.</p> <p>Luckily for us, we get a free instance of the AWS S3 Storage when we <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">use Cyclic</a>. No credit card is required.</p> <p><a href="https://deploy.cyclic.sh/ithink-corp/api" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><img alt="https://deploy.cyclic.app/button.svg" src="/content/62d6cf389192e7f60cbda7b0_button.svg"></a></p> <p>‍</p> <h2 id="vue-the-lightweight-framework"><a href="#vue-the-lightweight-framework" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Vue, the lightweight framework</h2> <p>Let's start by exploring the wonders of Vue, the framework that <a href="https://vuejs.org/about/faq.html#is-vue-fast" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">claims itself to be one of the most performant frontend frameworks</a>.</p> <h3 id="creating-a-new-project"><a href="#creating-a-new-project" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Creating a new project</h3> <p>It's no secret that setup is one of the most important stages in a project's lifecycle. It's the very first step in the journey that transforms an idea into a real-life, working application that runs on a modern computer.</p> <p>We can all agree that creating a boilerplate from scratch is exhausting. I mean, think about all the folders, files, and code that you'd need to keep repeating, forever. No one wants to do all that work!</p> <p>Luckily, Vue does all the work for us when we run the following command:</p> <p><code>npm init vue@latest</code></p> <p>It will ask you a bunch of questions so you can create the optimal setup that best fits your project. So go ahead, and accept/reject the following questions:</p> <ul> <li>Project name: <strong>ithink</strong></li> <li>TypeScript? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>JSX Support? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>Vue Router? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>Pinia? <strong>Yes</strong></li> <li>Vitest? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>Cypress? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>ESLint? <strong>No</strong></li> <li>Prettier? <strong>No</strong></li> </ul> <p>We'll see what each of these means throughout this article.</p> <p>Next up is installation. This time, you don't have to do anything. Just kick-back, relax, and wait for <code>yarn</code> to do its work! (of course, you can also use <code>npm</code> if that's your preference)</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-sh"><code><span class="token builtin class-name">cd</span> ithink <span class="token function">yarn</span> <span class="token function">install</span> <span class="token comment"># or npm install</span> </code></pre></div> <p>‍</p><p data-height="600" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="oNqxVBY" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:600px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/oNqxVBY"> vue-0</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span></p> <p></p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <p>This command will create a dead-simple boilerplate which comes with some defaults. Go ahead and run <code>yarn dev</code> or <code>npm run dev</code> and open up <code>http://localhost:3000</code> in your browser. It's already looking great, isn't it?</p> <p>You'll see a semi-usable application describing Vue, with the addition of some links to its inner-workings.</p> <p>Unfortunately, most of this stuff is useless to us. Therefore, we'll erase most of it so that we can continue along this guide:</p> <p>Take some time to observe the folder structure. Notice the emphasis that it places on <a href="https://jamstack.org/glossary/decoupling/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">decoupling</a>. Everything is where it's supposed to be, making it a very clean and elegant architecture to work on.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-text"><code>tree . ├── index.html ├── package.json ├── public │ └── favicon.ico ├── README.md ├── src │ ├── App.vue │ ├── components │ ├── index.css │ ├── main.js │ └── stores ├── vite.config.js └── yarn.lock </code></pre></div> <p>Don't worry if this looks intimidating. We'll cover <em>all of it</em> throughout this document.</p> <h3 id="configuring-seo"><a href="#configuring-seo" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Configuring SEO</h3> <p>You might have noticed that the title of our document is <em>"Vite App"</em>, with no immediately obvious way of changing it.</p> <p>It turns out that this is a great opportunity for us to delve into the first element: <code>index.html</code>. You've undoubtedly already seen this filename in a billion other places, but probably not in the context of Vue.</p> <p>So let's dive into <code>index.html</code>, and update some defaults:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token doctype"><span class="token punctuation"><!</span><span class="token doctype-tag">DOCTYPE</span> <span class="token name">html</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>html</span> <span class="token attr-name">lang</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>en<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>head</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>meta</span> <span class="token attr-name">charset</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation But notice that when you click on "post", the page reloads. This is the default <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">behavior of HTML forms</a>.</p> <p>Normally, we'd change that by calling <code>e.preventDefault</code>. But Vue focuses so much on simplicity that there's a super-convenient shortcut:</p> <p>‍</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">submit</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// TODO</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> ... <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>form</span> <span class="token attr-name">method</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>dialog<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span> <span class="token attr-name">@submit.prevent</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>submit<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> ... <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>form</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> ... <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>Would you look at that! We're able to shorten e.preventDefault() to @submit.prevent. Now, we don't even need to consider <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Event" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">the Event object</a> anymore!</p> <h3 id="tracking-a-loading-state"><a href="#tracking-a-loading-state" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Tracking a loading state</h3> <p>The user should know when their application is loading, whether it's posting new text to the server or just retrieving it.</p> <p>Let's create a variable that tracks when our component is sending/receiving data to/from the server. We're gonna be using <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reactive variables</a>.</p> <p>‍</p> <p>What is a <strong>reactive variable</strong>?</p> <ul> <li>Consider the following scenario:</li> </ul> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token keyword">let</span> a <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token number">4</span> <span class="token dom variable">document</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">getElementById</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'container'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">textContent</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> a <span class="token comment">// <p id="container">4</p></span> </code></pre></div> <ul> <li>Say that we updated the value in a to 5. One thing we know for sure is that the <code><p></code> element won't change. It will always say "4", unless we explicitly change it.</li> <li>Well, we don't have to! With <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/reactivity-fundamentals.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reactivity</a>, the DOM is automatically updated once the related variable is mutated.</li> <li>In Vue, reactive variables are created with ref, a function that takes any value and makes it reactive.</li> </ul> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code>‍<span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> a <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token number">4</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> a<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token number">5</span> </code></pre></div> <ul> <li>Notice the addition of .value. It's important, because if we did a = 5 we'd completely taking away the reactivity of the variable.</li> <li>Also, it doesn't matter that a is a constant variable, because we're only assigning to its .value property.</li> <li>Now look at the HTML:</li> </ul> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code>‍<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>{{ a }}<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <ul> <li>Vue will replace {{ a }} with its value: a.value, and the double-brackets are <em>not</em> optional.</li> </ul> <p>Okay, let's head right back into the submit logic. We'll create a new isLoading reactive variable, which will indicate when our app is in-contact with the server.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> isLoading <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token boolean">false</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token keyword">async</span> <span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">submit</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> isLoading<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">true</span>
<span class="token comment">// TODO: send data to server</span>
isLoading<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <h3 id="getting-user-input-from-form-elements"><a href="#getting-user-input-from-form-elements" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Getting user input from form elements</h3> <p>Our "new modal" component can't exist without the <code><textarea></code> form element. But this raises an important question: <em>how do we keep the javascript code in-sync with the DOM content?</em></p> <p>In a nutshell, Vue has a shortcut way of dealing with form elements. And it's quite convenient!</p> <p>As you can see, message is a reactive variable, so whenever the user types something into textarea, message will be instantly updated. That's the magic of v-model!</p> <p>Hey! You may be getting tired from typing .value all the time. Thankfully, Vue has plans to change that.</p> <h3 id="making-the-modal-inert-while-loading"><a href="#making-the-modal-inert-while-loading" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Making the modal inert while loading</h3> <p data-height="600" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="QWmNogz" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:600px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/QWmNogz"> vue-4</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span> </p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <p>When our app is loading (which is tracked by the isLoading variable that we saw in a previous section), we should disable interaction with it.</p> <p>This requires us getting access to a DOM element in JavaScript. The pure way of doing that is with body.querySelector(), but this approach is non-reactive. Plus, there's a simpler alternative offered by Vue:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token operator"><</span>script setup<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> container <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token keyword null nil">null</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>script<span class="token operator">></span>
<span class="token operator"><</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span>div ref<span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">"container"</span><span class="token operator">></span><span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>div<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> </code></pre></div> <p>These are called <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/template-refs.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">template refs</a>! And although it says null, Vue will fill container with the DOM element </p><div ref="container"> when it's created. It will also go back to null when it disappears.<p></p> <p>With this in hand, we can make our component inert while it's loading:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> container <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token keyword null nil">null</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">async</span> <span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">submit</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> isLoading<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">true</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> dialog<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">setAttribute</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"inert"</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token boolean">true</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token comment">// TODO: send data to server</span>
dialog<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">removeAttribute</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">"inert"</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> isLoading<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>div</span> <span class="token attr-name">ref</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>container<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>div</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>style</span> <span class="token attr-name">scoped</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token style"><span class="token language-css"> <span class="token selector">dialog<span class="token attribute"><span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token attr-name">inert</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span></span></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token atrule"><span class="token rule">@apply</span> filter brightness-90<span class="token punctuation">;</span></span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>style</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>Hey! While there's a simpler way to achieve the above (<code><div :inert="isLoading"></code>), I just had to create an opportunity to teach you about template refs, which are a pretty important feature in VueJS.</p> <h3 id="automatically-focusing-the-textarea"><a href="#automatically-focusing-the-textarea" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Automatically focusing the <code><textarea></code></h3> <p data-height="600" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="ExEKMQK" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:600px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/ExEKMQK"> vue-5</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span> </p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <p>When the user opens the NewModal component, we know that their objective is to input into the <code><textarea></code>. So, wouldn't it be convenient to save them the hassle of moving the cursor towards that form element?</p> <p>Let's implement this feature! Counter-intuitively, we can't do this:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>h1</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>blah blah<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>h1</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> textarea <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token keyword null nil">null</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
textarea<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">focus</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token comment">// this is WRONG!</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>textarea</span> <span class="token attr-name">ref</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>textarea<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>textarea</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>The above code won't work, because it's the same as saying null.focus().</p> <p>So, how do we tell Vue to only focus the textarea once it's available? The answer lies in <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/lifecycle.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><strong>lifecycle hooks</strong></a>.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/62e02ecd52420b19a8e6d301_lifecycle.png"></p> <p>We want to utilize the "mounted" hook, which is called right after the component is added to the DOM. That's when the <code><textarea></code> is shown, meaning that it's not null:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> onMounted <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span>
<span class="token function">onMounted</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> textarea<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">focus</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token comment">// CORRECT! :)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> </code></pre></div> <p>There are many more lifecycle hooks, and we usually use most of them. However, in our application, the "mounted" hook was more than enough. But just keep one thing in mind, you'll see this concept again and again in every framework.</p> <h3 id="closing-the-modal-when-clicked-outside"><a href="#closing-the-modal-when-clicked-outside" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Closing the modal when clicked outside</h3> <p data-height="600" data-default-tab="js,result" data-slug-hash="yLKOmKV" data-preview="true" data-user="eludapens" class="codepen" style="height:600px;box-sizing:border-box;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:2px solid;margin:1em 0;padding:1em"> <span>See the Pen <a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens/pen/yLKOmKV"> vue-6</a> by Eluda (<a href="https://codepen.io/eludapens">@eludapens</a>) on <a href="https://codepen.io">CodePen</a>.</span> </p> <script async src="https://cpwebassets.codepen.io/assets/embed/ei.js"></script> <p>It's a pretty common behavior in every modal to close it once the user clicks outside.</p> <p>In this step, we'll take a HUGE shortcut. Instead of manually implementing this behavior, we shall use another library to do it for us.</p> <p>The Vue community is humongous and infinitely helpful, so it's not a surprise to find a library like <a href="https://vueuse.org/functions" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@vueuse</a>: over 200 useful methods that cover almost every possible use–case.</p> <p>Our interest lies in the [onClickOutside event](<a href="https://vueuse.org/core/onClickOutside/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://vueuse.org/core/onClickOutside/</a>), which is triggered every time the user clicks outside a certain DOM element.</p> <p>After <a href="https://vueuse.org/guide/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">setting up @vueuse</a>, let's add it to our component:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token operator"><</span>script setup<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> onClickOutside <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'@vueuse/core'</span>
<span class="token comment">// Close dialog when clicked outside</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> container <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token keyword null nil">null</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token function">onClickOutside</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>container<span class="token punctuation">,</span> close<span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">close</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token comment">// TODO</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>script<span class="token operator">></span>
<span class="token operator"><</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span>dialog ref<span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">"container"</span><span class="token operator">></span><span class="token spread operator">...</span><span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>dialog<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> </code></pre></div> <p>Fascinating how in one line of code, we're able to implement such a seemingly complicating feature!</p> <h3 id="closing-the-modal"><a href="#closing-the-modal" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Closing the modal</h3> <p>The modal has no way of telling whether its opened or closed, as only its parent — App.vue — knows such information.</p> <p>But there's one thing we know to be true, and it's that the modal knows <em>when</em> it should be closed:</p> <ul> <li>user clicked outside,</li> <li>user submitted,</li> <li>user canceled.</li> </ul> <p>Therefore, we need a way for the child — NewModal — to communicate with its parent, App. And the solution is quite simple: <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/components/events.html" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Events</a>!</p> <p>With Vue, it's super-simple to define our own events, while dictating when they should be emitted, using <em>our</em> own rules.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token keyword">const</span> emit <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">defineEmits</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token string">'close'</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">close</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token function">emit</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'close'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Henceforth, whenever the modal needs to be closed, we emit the event "close" up into its parent.</p> <p>Hey! Notice how we didn't import defineEmits. That's because it's a compiler macro, so it's always there by default.</p> <h3 id="using-our-custom-component"><a href="#using-our-custom-component" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Using our custom component</h3> <p>Up until now, you couldn't see NewModal, because it hasn't been added to App.vue yet. So, let's change that:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token operator"><</span>script setup<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token maybe-class-name">NewModal</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'./components/NewModal.vue'</span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>script<span class="token operator">></span>
<span class="token operator"><</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token maybe-class-name">NewModal</span> <span class="token operator">/</span><span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> </code></pre></div> <p>With the code snippet above, the modal will always be open. So, let's add some toggle magic:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token operator"><</span>script setup<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token maybe-class-name">NewModal</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'./components/NewModal.vue'</span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> isModalOpen <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token boolean">false</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span>
<span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">openModal</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> isModalOpen<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">true</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">closeModal</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> isModalOpen<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">value</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token boolean">false</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>script<span class="token operator">></span>
<span class="token operator"><</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token maybe-class-name">NewModal</span> v<span class="token operator">-</span><span class="token keyword control-flow">if</span><span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">"isModalOpen"</span> <span class="token operator">/</span><span class="token operator">></span> <span class="token operator"><</span><span class="token operator">/</span>template<span class="token operator">></span> </code></pre></div> <p>We took advantage of <code>v-if</code> to show/hide the modal.</p> <p>And now we're done with the NewModal component. This one will display a list of items, and we don't know the length of that list before-hand.</p> <p>Let's create a new file at <code>src/ThoughtList.vue</code>. In Vue, here's how we repeat an element:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> items <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token string">'hello'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token string">'world!'</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>

It might be useful to split this component into two: <code>ThoughtList.vue</code> and <code>ThoughtItem.vue</code>.</p> <p>So, we'll change <code>src/ThoughtList.vue</code> to:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> ref <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'vue'</span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token maybe-class-name">ThoughtItem</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'./ThoughtItem.vue'</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> items <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">ref</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token string">'hello'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token string">'world!'</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>ul</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>li</span> <span class="token attr-name">v-for</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>item in items<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>ThoughtItem</span> <span class="token punctuation">/></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>li</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>ul</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>and the new <code>ThoughtItem.vue</code> will contain:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> Hello world! <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>And of course, don't forget to add it to <code>App.vue</code>:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token maybe-class-name">ThoughtList</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">"./components/ThoughtList.vue"</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>main</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>ThoughtList</span> <span class="token punctuation">/></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>main</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <h3 id="passing-text-from-parent-to-child"><a href="#passing-text-from-parent-to-child" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Passing text from parent to child</h3> <p>We've seen how to trigger events from child to parent, and now, it's time to <em>flip</em> that formula around.</p> <p>Currently, our <code>ThoughtItem</code> displays the same text: "Hello world!"</p> <p>But we want to show real data, which is held by the parent — <code>ThoughtList</code> — in the <code>items</code> reactive variable.</p> <p>The solution to this problem is called <strong>Props</strong> (properties). They're like HTML attributes, if they could contain <em>anything</em>! (arrays, objects, and even functions!)</p> <p>So let's make a little change to <code>ThoughtList.vue</code>:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>ul</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>li</span> <span class="token attr-name">v-for</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>item in items<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>ThoughtItem</span> <span class="token attr-name">:message</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">"</span>item<span class="token punctuation">"</span></span> <span class="token punctuation">/></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>li</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>ul</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>Hey! It's important to add the colon : before the prop name. It tells Vue to treat the content between "..." as JavaScript code (the item variable), instead of a String (the text "item").</p> <p>And now, we can access the text message in <code>ThoughtItem</code> effortlessly:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">setup</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> <span class="token function">defineProps</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">message</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token known-class-name class-name">String</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token comment">// `message` has type String.</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> {{ message }} <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>p</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> <span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>template</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>Hey! Just like defineEmits, defineProps is a compiler macro and doesn't require importing.</p> <h3 id="loading-data-from-the-server"><a href="#loading-data-from-the-server" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Loading data from the server</h3> <p>Up until now, we only used mock data. So, let's change that! We'll be getting data from an external API.</p> <p>But first, notice that we'll need to access our API from two separate components: ThoughtList for retrieving all items, and NewModal for adding new items to the <a href="https://docs.cyclic.sh/docs/concepts/database" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">l</a>ist.</p> <p>This is called a <a href="https://vuejs.org/guide/scaling-up/state-management.html#what-is-state-management" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">shared-state</a> between multiple components. There's no immediately obvious way of solving this issue, but thankfully, there's an entire library designed just for that, and it's called <a href="https://pinia.vuejs.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Pinia</a>.</p> <p>This is where we'll start working with the stores/ folder. So let's create the src/stores/thoughts.js file.</p> <p>‍</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/62e02ef269d01d02c0b009f1_pinia.png"></p> <p>‍</p> <p>A store should always resemble this boilerplate, so use it as a starting-point:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token comment">// thoughts.js</span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> defineStore <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'pinia'</span>

It's simply a collection of reactive variables and methods that act on them:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-javascript"><code><span class="token comment">// thoughts.js</span> <span class="token keyword module">import</span> <span class="token imports"><span class="token punctuation">{</span> defineStore <span class="token punctuation">}</span></span> <span class="token keyword module">from</span> <span class="token string">'pinia'</span>
<span class="token keyword module">export</span> <span class="token keyword module">default</span> <span class="token function">defineStore</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'thoughts'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token function">state</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">return</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token literal-property property">reactive_var</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token number">1</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">another_reactive_var</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token string">'awesome!'</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token literal-property property">again_another_reactive_var</span><span class="token operator">:</span> <span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token number">0</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token number">2</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token number">4</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">,</span>
